newsitem.title: USA: Miami puts single-member district plan on ballot.
newsitem.headline: Miami puts single-member district plan on ballot.

text.p: Miami voters will decide Sept 4 whether to abolish citywide commission elections in favor of single-member districts.

The ballot proposal was approved last week by the city commission. If approved, voters would elect a strong mayor who has veto powers over the five commissioners, who would be elected from single-member districts.
Currently, the mayor is one of five commissioners elected citywide and has no veto.
The proposal will go on the same ballot as the proposal to abolish the city and abosorb it into the Metro-Dade County government.
Elections supervisor David Leahy said there would be no conflict if voters approved both because the dissolution proposal would not take effect until September 1998.

"The city doesn't dissolve immediately, so this single-member district government would be in effect for the year while the city was in the process of dissolving," Leahy said Monday. "A new government would be the one phasing out the government."
The city commission has until Aug 15 to draft a plan specifying exactly how the dissolution would be carried out.

Commissioners adopted the single-member district proposal in hopes of helping ensure black representation on the commission, which is currently made up of four white Hispanics and one non-Hispanic white. They are still debating where the district boundaries should be drawn.
